basis: Latest PS6 DBSCAN hotspot and PS7 rider segment summaries.
source_data_limitation: Available records represent restaurant food delivery; use as a quick-commerce proxy only. Validate recommendations with actual quick-commerce operating data.

recommendations.title: Investigate the supported DBSCAN hotspot with the highest late rate
recommendations.observed_finding: DBSCAN hotspot 52 has the highest late rate among hotspots with at least the data-derived median support (85 orders).
recommendations.operational_problem: The supported hotspot has a higher observed late rate than the valid-GPS network benchmark; the available dataset does not identify the cause.
recommendations.recommended_management_action: Review dispatch timing, route conditions, and service coverage with local operators for this coordinate-defined hotspot. Verify the locality and current operations before changing footprint.
recommendations.expected_benefit_projected: Projected, not observed: a local review may identify operational adjustments worth testing; measure results in a follow-up pilot before attributing any change.

recommendations.title: Offer non-punitive workflow support to the highest late-rate rider segment
recommendations.observed_finding: Exploratory rider segment 0 (Higher late rate, slower deliveries, lower ratings, higher daily volume) has the highest segment-average late rate. The selected clustering silhouette is 0.247, indicating weak separation.

supporting_evidence.segment_description: Higher late rate, slower deliveries, lower ratings, higher daily volume

recommendations.operational_problem: One exploratory segment has a higher observed late rate; weak cluster separation means membership should not be treated as a definitive individual performance category.
recommendations.recommended_management_action: Use supportive, non-punitive workflow reviews with a representative sample of riders from this segment to understand barriers; do not make individual personnel decisions from clusters.
recommendations.expected_benefit_projected: Projected, not observed: reviewing operational barriers may suggest support improvements; assess any effect with later data and avoid causal attribution from this analysis.

recommendations.title: Pilot capacity review for the largest observed delivery hotspot
recommendations.observed_finding: DBSCAN hotspot 18 contains the largest valid-GPS order concentration (3187 orders; 7.60% of valid-GPS records). The highest-throughput rider segment averages 1.70 deliveries per active day.

supporting_evidence.source: PS6 DBSCAN hotspot summary and PS7 rider segment profile

recommendations.operational_problem: Recorded delivery demand is geographically concentrated, but current locality-level supply and quick-commerce demand are not available in this dataset.
recommendations.recommended_management_action: Pilot a limited staffing and service-coverage review around the largest observed hotspot, using rider throughput as context and validating local demand and current supply first.
recommendations.expected_benefit_projected: Projected, not observed: aligning planned coverage with verified demand may improve capacity fit; quantify any effect only after a pilot using actual quick-commerce records.
